question: For each search/fetch backend available here, which of the four required filters are natively supported, which are emulated client-side, and which are silently IGNORED when passed - established by sending a filter that MUST change the result set and checking whether it did?
answer:
SUCCESS:RES-0169 live differential matrix (same query with and without each filter).
NATIVE means the server-side parameter changed IDs or cardinality after a Jaccard<=0.5 or >=5% count rule.
IGNORED is recorded only after a positive-control filter on the same backend strongly changed results.
REJECTED means the filtered request returned HTTP >=400 instead of silently swallowing the param.
UNREACHABLE means this host had no authenticated session (Tavily 401, Exa 402, Brave 422, SearXNG localhost refused, DuckDuckGo HTML 202 challenge).
Client-side domain emulation on Wikipedia (post-filter URLs to arxiv.org) changed=True n=10->0; pass-through srdomain stayed IGNORED.

both_states_control.rule: IGNORED only if a filter that SHOULD change results did, and the candidate filter did not strongly change the set

client_emulation.method: post-filter en.wikipedia search URLs to netloc arxiv.org

availability.note: Key values were never printed. Commercial search APIs were probed unauthenticated only.

claims.claim: OpenAlex natively applies domain, language, region and recency filters: each of the four differentials strongly changed the /works transformer result set.
claims.independent_verification_path: Re-run OpenAlex unfiltered vs filter=language:de, institutions.country_code:jp, from_publication_date:2025-01-01, primary_location.source.id:s4306400194 and recompute Jaccard plus meta.count.

claims.claim: Wikipedia list=search language is NATIVE (en vs de hosts, disjoint pageids). Passing srdomain, region or srsince does not strongly change the en.wikipedia ID set after that positive control, so those three are IGNORED, not NATIVE.
claims.independent_verification_path: Compare wikipedia-en vs wikipedia-de (must change) then wikipedia-en vs wikipedia-srdomain/region/srsince (must not strongly change) using the stored capture pairs.

claims.claim: A filter is labelled IGNORED only after a positive-control filter that SHOULD change results did change them on the same backend. Wikipedia language is that control; Wikipedia domain is the ignored case.
claims.independent_verification_path: probe1_both_states.py recomputes both legs from captures and rejects a mutant that marks domain IGNORED without the language control.

claims.claim: Client-side domain emulation (keep only arxiv.org hosts from en.wikipedia search URLs) changes the result set to empty, while the same filter passed as srdomain is IGNORED. Emulation is therefore a client behaviour, not evidence the backend honoured the param.
claims.independent_verification_path: Rebuild Wikipedia search URLs from stored titles and post-filter netloc==arxiv.org; require n_after=0 and srdomain Jaccard not strongly changed.

claims.claim: Crossref honours from-pub-date and issn filters (NATIVE recency and domain/venue) and REJECTS filter=language:de and extra region=DE with HTTP 400 rather than silently ignoring them.
claims.independent_verification_path: Re-hash crossref-unfiltered vs crossref-recency/domain (200, counts move) and crossref-language/region (400 bodies).

claims.claim: PubMed ESearch language (german[la]), recency (pdat 2025+) and journal domain (Nature[ta]) are NATIVE by cardinality even when the top-10 PMIDs stay put; extra region=DE is IGNORED at the same count as unfiltered after that control.
claims.independent_verification_path: Compare esearchresult.count on pubmed-unfiltered vs pubmed-language/recency/domain/region from stored JSON.

claims.claim: Tavily, Exa, Brave Search, local SearXNG and DuckDuckGo HTML are UNREACHABLE on this host (401 missing key, 402 payment, 422 missing x-subscription-token, connection refused, 202 anomaly page). Docs that list include_domains or time_range do not make those filters NATIVE here.
claims.independent_verification_path: Re-read auth-tavily/exa/brave/searxng/ddg captures; a NATIVE cell for those backends must fail well_formed.

claims.claim: Tavily's published search schema lists include_domains, country, language and start_date/end_date, but that is a docs claim only: without a live differential on this host the support class remains UNREACHABLE/INFERRED, not NATIVE.
claims.independent_verification_path: Re-fetch docs.tavily.com search endpoint HTML and confirm include_domains; do not promote to NATIVE unless a key-backed differential is captured.

claims.claim: arXiv API recency via submittedDate is NATIVE; extra language/region/domain query params return HTTP 200 with identical ID sets after that control and are therefore silently IGNORED.
claims.independent_verification_path: Recompute arxiv-unfiltered vs arxiv-recency (must change) and vs arxiv-language/region/domain (Jaccard 1).

claims.claim: GitHub repository search language:rust and created:>2025-01-01 are NATIVE. Extra domain=arxiv.org and region=DE query params leave total_count and IDs unchanged and are IGNORED. HN Algolia numericFilters recency is NATIVE; extra language/country/domain params are REJECTED with HTTP 400 Unknown parameter.
claims.independent_verification_path: Recompute github-unfiltered vs github-language/recency/domain/region and hn-unfiltered vs hn-recency/language/region/domain from captures.

reviewers.notes: Defaults to REFUTED unless a stored differential pair recomputes to the claimed verdict.
Docs-only commercial filter lists stay INFERRED; NATIVE without strongly_changed is rejected.

residual_unknowns: Authenticated Tavily/Exa/Brave/SearXNG sessions were not exercised; their native-vs-ignored map remains unknown on this host.
DuckDuckGo HTML returned a 202 challenge page, so kl/df/site: were not classified.
Bibliographic domain is venue/source-id (ISSN, Nature[ta], OpenAlex source), not a web Host header.
strongest_surviving_counterargument: Wikipedia ranking jitter can move one pageid between sequential calls, so a naive ID inequality would over-claim NATIVE for undocumented params; the Jaccard<=0.5 / 5% cardinality rule is what keeps srdomain IGNORED.
